package_info.why_malicious: Both packages contain setup.py files with base64-encoded payloads that, when decoded and executed during installation, download and execute a batch script from a Discord CDN. This script escalates privileges, disables security controls, collects sensitive system and user data, exfiltrates it via Discord webhooks, and downloads further malware. The packages are clear typosquats of popular libraries, and all observed behaviors are consistent with credential theft and system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code decodes a base64 string and executes it, which downloads a batch file from a Discord CDN to the user's temp directory and executes it silently.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing obfuscated (base64-encoded) code during installation that downloads and runs remote scripts is a classic malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only perform package installation, not download and execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some legitimate packages may download dependencies, but never via obfuscated code or from Discord CDN.
key_indicators: os.system call with decoded remote command
Download and execution of remote batch file from Discord CDN

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the batch script checks for administrative privileges and relaunches itself with elevated permissions using PowerShell if not already running as admin.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often attempts to escalate privileges to bypass security controls and access sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Installer scripts should not attempt to escalate privileges or relaunch themselves as admin.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may request elevation, but not in this obfuscated or hidden manner.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
echo function CHECK_IF_ADMIN { > powershell.ps1
... (see full code in report) ...
powershell.exe -executionpolicy bypass -windowstyle hidden -noninteractive -nologo -file powershell.ps1
del powershell.ps1 /f /q
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The batch script writes a PowerShell script to disk, which disables Windows Defender, creates persistence via scheduled tasks, collects system and user data, and exfiltrates it to a Discord webhook. It then executes the PowerShell script with execution policy bypassed and deletes the script.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security controls, establishing persistence, and exfiltrating data are all hallmarks of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Installer scripts should not disable security, create persistence, or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; these actions are never legitimate in package installation.
key_indicators: Execution policy bypass and script self-deletion

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The PowerShell script collects system info, IP, UUID, MAC, browser data, Discord tokens, and more, compresses it, and exfiltrates it to a Discord webhook. It also downloads and executes further malware (main.exe) from GitHub, then cleans up traces.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Comprehensive data theft, exfiltration, and anti-forensics (cleanup) are clear indicators of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should collect and exfiltrate user/system data or download and run further malware.
key_indicators: Data collection: system info, browser data, tokens
Download and execution of remote executable

attack_chain.action: User installs the package, triggering setup.py execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Base64-decoded command downloads and executes batch script.

attack_chain.action: Batch script checks for admin privileges and relaunches itself as admin if needed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Batch script proceeds to create and execute PowerShell script.

attack_chain.action: Batch script writes a PowerShell script to disk, disables Defender, creates persistence, and executes the PowerShell script.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell script collects and exfiltrates data, downloads further malware.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell script collects sensitive data, exfiltrates it to Discord webhook, downloads and runs additional malware, and cleans up traces.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise and data theft complete.

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall download and execution of remote scripts
Creation of scheduled tasks for persistence
Collection and exfiltration of system/user data via Discord webhook
Download and execution of remote executables
file_indicators: References to Discord CDN or Discord webhooks in scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for base64-decoded command execution in setup.py during package installation. Flag any postinstall scripts that download and execute remote files, especially from Discord CDN or GitHub. Detect attempts to add Windows Defender exclusions, create scheduled tasks named 'KDOT', or exfiltrate data to Discord webhooks. Look for creation and deletion of suspicious files in %temp% and %APPDATA%/KDOT. Network monitoring should alert on connections to Discord CDN, Discord webhooks, and suspicious GitHub repositories.
